thesis: SOL runs into the Breakpoint window over the next two weeks. ETF filings and treasury companies keep buying, and smart money on chain has been accumulating since the last dip. Invalidation: if SOL loses 180 on a daily close or smart money netflow turns negative for a week, I am out.

qa.q: If the Breakpoint bid is real, why hold SOL itself rather than the ecosystem names that usually beta up harder into that window?
qa.a: Liquidity. I can size SOL on a perp with tight spreads and get out in one click. Ecosystem beta has thinner books and I have been trapped in them before.

qa.q: Breakpoint run-ups are a well known pattern. What tells you this one is still forming rather than already priced in by everyone waiting for it?
qa.a: Funding is flat and open interest has not expanded yet, so the crowd is not leaning long. If it were priced I would expect funding to be elevated and OI near the highs.

qa.q: You said two weeks. Do you exit into Breakpoint itself or hold through the event, and what would make you take profit early?
qa.a: I sell into the headlines. Breakpoint is the event, not the catalyst. The daily close above 180 has to hold on every day of the window or I am out early.

qa.q: What counts as smart money netflow turning negative, whose wallets and whose dashboard, and would you actually act on it if price held above 180?
qa.a: Nansen smart money netflow on SOL, seven day window. Threshold is a negative seven day netflow of more than ten million dollars. Yes I trust it over price, flows lead in my experience.
